A homeowner searching for “plumber near me,” a property manager looking for a reliable go-to contractor for their tenants, and a real estate agent racing to fix something before the open house. Contractor SEO is what enables them to find you.


They all search online. Search engine optimization is based on several algorithms. Criteria they consider, among hundreds of additional factors, are how strong your client reviews are, how fast your site loads, and whether you’re using the right keywords to connect with searchers in your geographical service area.


Visibility in the online search platforms matters more than ever for contractors. There are literally billions of searches online every day, and search volume has continually been increasing year after year. Among all Google searches,[46%](https://www.shopify.com/blog/local-seo-statistics) have local intent.

## **SEO for Contractors: What You Need to Know**


In this guide, you’ll learn about local SEO for contractors and how to use SEO to acquire new customers in your area. Contractor SEO involves a number of different search optimization tactics and activities, including:


- On-page optimization
- Service and location pages in your website
- Technical SEO
- Inclusion in the Google local pack
- Google Business Profile
- Online directories
- Customer reviews
- Content strategy


Contractor SEO involves targeting keywords to rank high in search engines such as Google and Bing. For an SEO deep dive, use this[local SEO guide for small businesses](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-search/) .


SEO, though, is evolving… Today, SEO also includes visibility in the AI answer platforms, such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity. This is called AEO (answer engine optimization) or GEO (generative engine optimization). The good news is that there is a great deal of overlap between traditional SEO and AI SEO.


[SEO, AEO, and GEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/seo-vs-aeo-vs-geo-why-its-all-still-seo/) run on many of the same fundamentals as SEO. If you get your contractor SEO strategies right, you are already covering most of AEO/GEO too. For a closer look at what is specifically relevant for AEO/GEO, see this guide:[AI search optimization for local businesses](https://www.thryv.com/blog/ai-search-optimization-for-local-business/) .


## Why is Local SEO Important for Contractors?


Local contractor SEO is important because generating leads online is your bread and butter. It’s how new customers find you.


Your prospective customers are searching on Google. A lot.


As mentioned, roughly 46% of Google searches have local intent. According to Ahrefs, there are 427 million “near me” searches in the United States monthly. There are currently 844,000 monthly searches for “HVAC near me” and related terms, 709,000 for “plumber near me,” and 381,000 for “electrician near me.”


It’s clear that your audience is looking for local contractors.


Do it right, and you’re the one who shows up when a potential customer searches. Do it wrong, and someone else gets the call, and you lose the job and the ongoing business. Simple as that.


Another reason why SEO is important compared to other marketing options for contractors is that organic search is cost-effective and the results compound over time.


The[ROI of SEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/hidden-roi-seo-services-for-small-businesses-2026/) is one of the highest of any forms of marketing. Whereas advertising requires a continual outflow of ad spend (or the ads stop running), once your organic visibility gains traction, it’s much easier to maintain the visibility at a mere fraction of the cost of advertising. If you’re ranking #1 for “24 hour plumbers in Omaha” today, chances are that you’ll rank towards the top of Google for months to come.


Another reason that contractor SEO is important for your marketing is that Google tends to favor local specialists over national generalists for searches with local intent. If you type “emergency plumber in Chicago” or “organic landscaping services near me” in Google, you’re likely to see a number of local plumbers and landscapers, respectively, in the search results page.


## **8 SEO Tips for Contractors**


Many factors go into contractor SEO. However, if you’re looking for effective quick tips to improve your results, below are eight local SEO action items to get you started.


### **1. Claim and Optimize Your Local Contractor Business Listings**


The first step for contractors to build local visibility is to claim and verify business profiles on[Google Business Profiles](https://business.google.com/us/business-profile/) (GBP). These listings act as digital storefronts, so you show up in local listings.


**Claim your local Google Business Profile.**


If you haven’t, create or claim your company on Google Business Profile with this[detailed, step-by-step overview](https://www.thryv.com/blog/set-up-google-business-profile/) . Add as much information as possible, and keep your profile accurate over time. Once consumers find map and business listings, a whopping[90% of searchers buy within a week](https://wiserreview.com/blog/local-seo-statistics/) of their local query.


For you as a contractor, this is[one of the biggest opportunities](https://www.thryv.com/blog/near-me-search-local-seo-opportunities/) to show up in local listings when someone searches for “electrician near me” or “carpenter near me.”


Check out this[Google Business Profile Guide](https://www.thryv.com/guides-resources/the-ultimate-google-business-profile-guide/?utm_medium=website&utm_source=blog&utm_campaign=leadpage) to learn how to show up higher in search and connect with your customers.


**Get listed in local directories.**


Other sites will also create profiles for your business. These are called[directories](https://www.thryv.com/blog/32-business-listing-sites-that-will-get-you-referral-traffic/) , and there are dozens, if not hundreds, of them for contractors. For example,[Thumbtack](https://www.thumbtack.com/) ,[HomeAdvisor](https://www.homeadvisor.com/) ,[Yelp](https://www.yelp.com/) , and[Angi](https://www.angi.com/) .


Add your business to as many as possible to maximize your online presence. AI search engines like ChatGPT and Claude verify information from external resources. Keep your[local business listing management](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-business-listings-management/) updated, so information like name, address, business description, services, and phone number matches across all sites.


### **2. Add the Right Keywords to Your Website**


When people talk about SEO, AEO, and GEO, you’ll see the term “[keyword research](https://www.thryv.com/blog/how-to-do-basic-keyword-research/) ” thrown around often. Keywords are words or phrases that people search for in Google or enter in AI search engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. For example, “best contractor near me” is a keyword. If you know which keywords your customers are searching for, you can update your website to target those searches.


Here’s an example from a[local construction website](https://www.palacioconstruction.com/bathroom-remodel) :


[Source](https://www.palacioconstruction.com/bathroom-remodel)


These pages tell both people and Google what services you offer. It improves[customer experience](https://www.thryv.com/blog/customer-experience-101/) and helps you rank higher in searches.


Use keywords that best describe your business. Be straightforward; use commonly known terms – not any jargon, punny, or fancy terms. Apply these keywords to your website, especially in the navigation and large page headlines, since they count more there. Also, be detailed about the type of work you offer, the locations you serve, licenses, pricing, and contact information.


Use this guide to learn[how to do keyword research](https://www.thryv.com/blog/how-to-do-basic-keyword-research/) .


### **3. Create Location Pages to Show the Areas You Serve**


Like service pages, location pages help you appear in[local searches](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-search/) . Local searches are keywords specific to areas, like “best contractor in Arizona.”


You can rank for these keywords by creating location pages that explain where your company operates. Let’s go back to that last example:


[Source](https://www.palacioconstruction.com/bathroom-remodel)


This website lists the different locations where the company works. Each option has a link to an individual page that tells you more about that service area:


[Source](https://www.palacioconstruction.com/bathroom-remodel)


Create one page for each service area you cover. Use the city/region name in the URL, title tag, and H1. Customize the pages as much as possible with local names or characteristics of the area, so the pages don’t sound templated where you only swap out names.


**Tip:**[Website builders](https://www.thryv.com/features/professional-website/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) have customizable templates you can use for easier creation of location pages.


### **4. Encourage Customers to Write Online Reviews**


[Online reviews](https://www.thryv.com/blog/why-reviews-matter/) are your online reputation. They can make or break your contractor SEO efforts. They provide the trustworthy data search engines rely on to evaluate a contractor’s reputation and recommend them to searchers. Even[responding to negative reviews](https://www.thryv.com/blog/respond-negative-customer-reviews-online/) shows Google that your profile is active.


Ask customers for reviews, and don’t be shy! Email your customers with a link to your profile on Yelp, Google Business Profile, Houzz, etc., and respond to the reviews – even the negative ones. Important: Try to spread reviews across multiple online review sites, not all reviews on one site. It matters because search engines source data across many different sites. The more that you’re well represented on multiple sites, the more credibility you’ll have in their eyes.


Make it easy for your customers to find your Google Business Profile so that they can leave you a review. Use the free[Google Review Link Generator](https://www.thryv.com/google-review-link-generator/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) to create one direct link straight to your review screen, so more of your requests turn into real reviews.

### **5. Build Trust and Loyalty with Your Customers**


When someone hires a local contractor for the first time, they are not just getting a repair or installation done. They are trusting a stranger to come into their home or touch their valuable belongings, and get fairly charged for it.


That’s why trust gets you the job before you even pick up the phone. Potential customers trust you not only because of customer reviews, but also because of the trust symbols you showcase on your website. Once you earn their trust, it turns into repeat business and deep loyalty. Your online presence isn’t just how people find you. It’s how they decide whether to trust you before they’ve never met you.


Show off[common trust symbols](https://www.thryv.com/blog/trust-symbols-trust/) on your contractor website, e.g., recognition from local industry associations, industry awards, industry badges, quotes from experts who mentioned your business, and testimonials from customers. Furthermore, add project photos, mention your rates, list your phone number visibly, and insert your headshot.


**Tip** : Research uncommon ways to[build trust](https://www.thryv.com/blog/uncommon-ways-build-trust/) .


### **6. Review Your On-page and Technical SEO**


Keep your website technically sound and fresh with new content. Both signal to search engines that the business is active. Frequent content updates also build credibility with clients, demonstrating that the business is responsive and attentive to customer needs.


When creating content for your website, follow a few foundational SEO and AEO/GEO best practices. These details will make your site easier for Google and AI search engines to read and analyze, giving you a better chance of ranking for different keywords.


This is where things can get pretty technical. To keep it simple, here are the basics to focus on when creating site content.


- **Content quality:** Create valuable content that provides helpful information for readers. Don’t be salesy; give insights that build trust and loyalty. Add images, links to relevant resources, and videos of your business helping customers. If you want to[outrank your competition](https://www.thryv.com/blog/how-to-beat-your-competition-in-business/) , your website’s content must be as good as your actual work.
- **Questions:** Include commonly asked questions in your content writing and answer them immediately. Add[FAQ pages](https://www.thryv.com/blog/why-every-small-business-needs-a-faq-page-in-2026/) .
- **Links:** Spread the good “[link juice](https://www.thryv.com/blog/ink-juice/) ” by inter-linking pages with each other. Where appropriate, link to external websites to deliver a delightful experience.
- **Schema Markup:** Apply ‘LocalBusiness’[Schema markup](https://www.thryv.com/blog/schema-markup-for-small-businesses-aeo-guide/) to your content. It is in the HTML code and tells search engines and AI tools details about your business, such as location, service area, phone number, and business hours. This increases your chances of showing up in local search results,[featured snippets, and AI answers](https://www.thryv.com/blog/optimize-website-for-featured-snippets-ai-answers/) .
- **Page Structure:** Apply header tags (H1, H2, H3, etc.) to page headlines to organize content into different sections. This shows Google what to focus on on your page. Use page-relevant keywords in these headers. To achieve stronger results in the AI answer engines, structure some of your headers as the questions that your customers are likely typing into the AI platforms.
- **Titles & Meta Descriptions:** Decide which keyword to target and aim to rank for each page. Use these target keywords in title tags and meta descriptions, as those are what Google displays in the search results page to your prospective customers.
- **Site Speed:** Make your page load time as fast as possible; aim for around one second. Avoid large images and files that take time to load. These delays will affect your search rankings as well as the user experience.
- **HTML Code:** Google and AI search engines read the HTML code behind your page, not the page as you see it. Keep your code clean and include the right labeling, such as alt tags and title tags, etc.
- **URL Structure:** The URL, or web address, for pages matters a lot. Make sure they include your target keywords, like “www.website.com/ **remodeling-services** ”
- **Mobile-Friendly:** Your site should automatically reformat for different screen dimensions, so people can read it in a[mobile-friendly](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-does-mobile-friendly-mean-6-definitions/) way on their handheld devices.


**To do:** Update your website regularly. A fresh website ranks higher than one that looks old and outdated. Publish blogs with insights from your industry. Make them educational, not salesy, to build search engine trust and attract new leads.


**Tip** : Perform regular[SEO site audits](https://www.thryv.com/blog/fall-seo-cleanup-small-business-guide/) to keep your site fresh and rank where your customers are searching.


### **7. Partner with Other Local Businesses**


Your site will be much more credible if other websites link to it. This is called “backlinking,” and it’s very valuable for local contractor SEO.


Backlinking is one of the tougher things to do online, but here’s what I recommend:


1. **Partner with other local businesses** . Find ways to trade links on your sites that benefit both you and your partners.
2. **Add links to your site on different profiles** . Think social media, directories, events, and review sites. Even if no one clicks them, those links still matter. An active, consistent social media presence also helps AI search tools verify your business information.
3. **Create awesome content** . If you create cool and compelling content, people will share it online.


Contact 5 local, non-competing businesses in your area and ask to link to each other’s sites. Each backlink counts as a “vote” of confidence in your business. Then check whether your social media sites, industry directories, and review profiles already have correct links back to your site.


Consider cross-promoting deals with other businesses to improve your backlinking strategy.


### **8. Track and Improve Your Website Performance Over Time**


Finally, track your SEO performance. Tools like[Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/about) and[Google Analytics](https://developers.google.com/analytics) help you see what’s working and what’s not.[Thryv Search Boosts](https://www.thryv.com/boosts/search-engine-optimization/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=OrganicSocial) monitor calls, clicks, GBP performance, keyword rankings, and backlinks.


SEO expert[Michael Brazile](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-brazile-1256a32/) compares SEO to a cruise ship. It doesn’t move as fast as a motorboat, and it’s not nimble like a jet ski. It’s slow and powerful, but it can take you far if you point it in the right direction. How do you know if you’re going the right way? Monitoring keyword rankings, Google traffic, and backlinks pointing to your site tells you whether your SEO strategy is working. Monitoring your brand visibility and citations in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and the other AI answer engines tells you if your AEO/GEO strategy is effective.


And ultimately, check your SEO ROI in real numbers: calls, leads, and revenue.


Check your analytics at least once a month to see which pages and keywords are attracting visitors to your website and driving conversions.


## **A Winning SEO Strategy for Contractors**


The most effective SEO strategy for contractors is to **focus on local searches** . You want to get that call precisely at the time someone is searching for a local contractor.


### **Quick Recap: 8 Steps to Achieve Better Local SEO Results**


1. Claim and optimize your local contractor business listings. Keep Google Business Profile and other directory listings accurate, consistent, and updated.


2. Add the right keywords to your website. Describe your services in commonly used terms. Avoid fancy terms, jargon, or jokes.


3. Create location pages to show the areas you serve. Build location pages for each service area you work in. This increases visibility for “near me” searches, as well.


4. Encourage customers to write online reviews. Ask customers for online reviews. Spread them across multiple platforms, and respond to reviews (even the bad ones).


5. Build trust and loyalty with your customers. Add badges, testimonials, and project photos so prospective customers trust you before they call.


6. Review your on-page and technical SEO. Get your website up to the latest technical standards.


7. Partner with other local businesses. Trade links with local businesses.


8. Track and improve your website performance over time. Use tools to track what’s working and what’s not.
